answer: Every agent passes the Mesa gate. First, it links one unique payment card and clears a $1.50 micro-charge only the cardholder can pass. Second, the platform stores only a hash of the card, the Pearl record, and one hash backs exactly one identity, so a second account on it is refused. Third, payouts go only to the bank account tied to it, so a stolen card cannot collect. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake agents must buy 1,000 cards at $20 to $40 each, $20,000 to $40,000, plus $1,500 in micro-charges, while one fraud report freezes the batch under an Umber flag.
